news.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
news.lede: Spain head coach hits out at ‘acts of aggression’. Fifa investigation into incident yet to result in sanctions. Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final. At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history.

news.title: Guardiola snubs Italy! Manager chooses personal break over rebuilding Azzurri after World Cup failures
news.lede: Pep Guardiola has formally turned down the opportunity to become Italy's next national team manager despite the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) making him its leading candidate to rebuild the Azzurri after another disappointing FIFA World Cup campaign. Football News: Pep Guardiola has turned down the opportunity to manage Italy's national football team, choosing to prioritize a personal break over rebuilding the Azzurri after their World Cup failures. Reports reveal the Italian Football Federation's efforts to persuade him, but Guardiola remains committed to his decision for time away from football.

news.title: Aston Villa reject Serie A club’s ‘tiny offer’ for World Cup finalist
news.lede: Aston Villa have turned down Juventus’ ‘tiny offer’ for Emiliano Martinez, per journalist Gianluca Di Marzio. The Serie A club are looking to sign a new goalkeeper to compete with Michele Di Gregorio for the starting role. They submitted a bid worth around £5 million for Martinez, which was quickly rebuffed. Villa are under no immediate pressure to sell, as the Argentinian is under contract until 2029.

news.title: Bayern Munich star Michael Olise plays in NYC pickup game
news.lede: You have to give it to Bayern Munich and France superstar Michael Olise, the man does love football. Well, after France lost the third-place game at the World Cup to England, the 24-year-old could not stay away from the game for long, so he joined a pickup game in New York City. Imagine you are stretching trying to get loose after sitting in a cube all day pouring through spreadsheets and you look across the field and have to defend Olise. Not just Olise, though, but Olise wearing some wild pants.

news.title: How World Cup 2026 proved football has remarkable ability to cure all ills
news.lede: The trophy safely on display at the Spanish FA headquarters, England’s wounds no longer so raw, and the annual football calendar now into its miniscule vacuum, you’re left to reflect on the past six weeks and ponder whether the 2026 edition in the United States, Canada and Mexico was a resounding success or an unmitigated flop. This one really could have gone either way. The expansion from 32 teams to 48 had the potential for greater drama but also the risk of suffocating, of making the World Cup the one thing it should never be: tedious. Would North America buy into soccer in a way we hadn’t seen at USA 1994?

news.title: World Cup match-fixing probe sparked after suspicious Spain match
news.lede: One of Spain’s matches on their way to winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup became the subject of a match-fixing probe. Spain won the tournament thanks to a 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final, having triumphed in all but one of their seven matches on their way to the climax at MetLife Stadium. The exception was a goalless draw with Cape Verde in their opening match of the World Cup, and the game was flagged as suspicious by the Council of Europe's betting monitoring unit, the Group of Copenhagen. Investigators were thought to be left surprised that Cape Verde managed to hold Spain to a goalless draw, and the match was played on ‘yellow notice’, meaning further investigation was required.
